steps.evidence: README.md:124-130 (local Supabase stack in Docker; applies supabase/migrations and seed.sql)

notes: npm per README and package-lock.json (v3); no CI workflows (.github only has funding.yaml). .env.local must hold real local-Supabase values: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL (the API URL), NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, all from `supabase status`. LLM provider keys are optional (users can enter them in the UI). The Supabase stack (Postgres, auth, storage, studio on :54323) runs through the Supabase CLI on Docker, not docker compose. Migrations are applied by `supabase start` itself. The README's SQL edit step comes after `supabase start` has already applied that migration, so it only takes effect after `npm run db-reset`. The README says it prevents storage-file deletion issues, so it is not needed for the app to start. `npm run chat` = supabase start && npm run db-types && next dev; plain `npm run dev` also works once Supabase is up. Node: the README says 'i.e. v18', while .nvmrc pins v20.11.0. npm install runs `husky install` via prepare.
